judgments.justification: “Outperformed it on five of the six datasets” is wrong; Larchmont-GNN was higher on all six.
It reports “79.4 vs 78.4,” correctly giving Larchmont-GNN a 1.0-point average advantage.
“Higher on five of six datasets, except Hollin-Sol” is wrong; Avonlea was higher on four, while Larchmont also led Jessamine-Kin.
It correctly reports reductions to “78.7,” “78.9,” and “78.0” after removing ring pooling, distance features, or both.
The passage does not mention the absence of statistical tests or limits on statistical-significance claims.
It correctly describes Larchmont as “slightly larger and slower” than Quintrell, far more efficient than Avonlea, and requiring no pretraining.
Although “79.4 vs 78.4” is correct, “five of the six datasets” misreports the all-six-dataset advantage.
It explicitly conveys a small margin on Lumley-Metab: “69.8 vs 69.5.”
